title: An Expert's Guide to Training Physics-informed Neural Networks
authors_full: Sifan Wang, Shyam Sankaran, Hanwen Wang, Paris Perdikaris
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA 19104, USA (S. Wang and H. Wang: Graduate Group in Applied Mathematics and Computational Science; Sankaran and Perdikaris: Department of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics)
subdomain: PINN training pipeline (non-dimensionalization, Fourier features, RWF, loss balancing, causal/curriculum training) + forward-PDE benchmark suite
industry_context: Academic/computational science and engineering broadly; funded by US Department of Energy (ASCR DE-SC0019116, ASDMAP DE-AR0001201), US Air Force AFOSR FA9550-20-1-0060; Predictive Intelligence Lab, UPenn
physics_enforced_exact: Seven benchmark PDE systems (Sec. 7): (1) Allen-Cahn: u_t - 0.0001 u_xx + 5u^3 - 5u = 0, t in [0,1], x in [-1,1]; (2) advection: u_t + c u_x = 0, c = 80, periodic on (0,2pi); (3) Stokes flow: -nu Delta u + Grad p = 0, Grad . u = 0, 2D pipe with cylinder obstacle (r=0.05, Re=20 via U*=0.2, L*=0.1); (4) Kuramoto-Sivashinsky: u_t + alpha u u_x + beta u_xx + gamma u_xxxx = 0 with alpha=100/16, beta=100/16^2, gamma=100/16^4, periodic on (0,2pi); (5) lid-driven cavity: incompressible Navier-Stokes in non-dimensional form u . Grad u + Grad p - (1/Re) Delta u = 0, Grad . u = 0, Re=3200; (6) Navier-Stokes flow in a torus: velocity-vorticity formulation w_t + u . Grad w = (1/Re) Delta w, Grad . u = 0, Re=100, Omega=[0,2pi]^2, T=10; (7) Navier-Stokes flow around a cylinder: u_t + u Grad u + Grad p - nu u = 0, Grad . u = 0 (rho=1, nu=0.001, U=1.5, Re=100)
dimensionality: 1D+time (Allen-Cahn, advection, Kuramoto-Sivashinsky) and 2D steady / 2D+time (Stokes pipe, lid-driven cavity, NS torus, NS cylinder)
nonlinearity: strongly nonlinear in most benchmarks (Allen-Cahn cubic reaction 5u^3-5u, KS quadratic convection alpha u u_x, NS convective term u.Grad u at Re up to 3200); includes linear/elliptic cases (advection c=80, Stokes flow)
bcs_ic_handled: Initial conditions as penalty loss L_ic against g(x) (for NS cylinder the IC is taken from a coarse 4-second numerical simulation); boundary conditions: periodic BCs imposed exactly (hard) via a special Fourier feature embedding v(x)=[cos(omega x), sin(omega x)], omega=2pi/P (Dong & Ni), extended to 2D and to time-periodicity with trainable period P_t; Dirichlet/Neumann/Robin as penalty loss L_bc (no-slip walls, parabolic inflow u_in=4Uy(0.41-y)/0.41^2, outflow v d n - p n = 0 for Stokes/NS); other BC types can also be hard-imposed by modifying network outputs (distance functions, refs [65,66])
enforcement_mechanism: hybrid: soft-penalty residual losses (autodiff PDE residual, IC and general BC terms) combined with hard-constraint exact periodic boundary conditions via Fourier feature construction
enforcement_details: Physics enters as the mean-square PDE residual R_theta(t,x) = d u_theta/dt + N[u_theta] evaluated by JAX automatic differentiation at randomly sampled collocation points (Eq. 2.4, 2.8); composite loss L = lambda_ic L_ic + lambda_bc L_bc + lambda_r L_r (Eq. 2.9); temporal domain partitioned into M equal segments with causal temporal weights w_i = exp(-eps * sum_{k<i} L_r^k) (Eq. 2.11), frozen w.r.t. theta via jax stop_gradient; global weights updated every f=1000 steps by gradient-norm balancing (Eq. 2.12-2.14) or diagonal-NTK balancing (Eq. 5.4-5.9), combined by moving average lambda_new = alpha*lambda_old + (1-alpha)*lambda_new; pre-processing non-dimensionalization of PDE system; random weight factorization W = diag(exp(s)) . V; modified MLP with two input encoders U, V merged by point-wise multiplication (Eq. 6.7-6.11)
network_architecture: MLP backbone; recommended width 128-512 and depth 3-6 (Sec. 4.1); modified MLP (Wang et al. [26]) with two encoders U=sigma(W1 x + b1), V=sigma(W2 x + b2), each hidden layer g^(l) = sigma(f^(l)) . U + (1 - sigma(f^(l))) . V (Eq. 6.8-6.9); random weight factorization applied to all weight matrices; ablation default 4 hidden layers x 256 neurons; best configurations up to 5 layers x 256 (Tables 6-13)
activation_function: tanh (recommended; hyperbolic tangent; GeLU used for the Stokes flow case; sinusoidal and GeLU noted as alternatives; ReLU rejected because its second-order derivative is zero)
input_representation: non-dimensionalized spatio-temporal coordinates (t, x) passed through random Fourier feature embeddings gamma(x) = [cos(Bx), sin(Bx)] with B ~ N(0, sigma^2), recommended sigma in [1,10]; time-periodic variant w(t,x) = [cos(omega_t t), sin(omega_t t), v(t,x)] with omega_t = 2pi/P_t and trainable P_t
output_representation: latent solution fields: scalar u (Allen-Cahn, advection, KS); velocity u=(u,v) and pressure p for Stokes/cavity/cylinder; velocity (u,v) and vorticity w = Curl x u for the torus case; hard BC modifications possible on outputs
loss_terms: L(theta) = lambda_ic L_ic(theta) + lambda_bc L_bc(theta) + lambda_r L_r(theta) (Eq. 2.9); L_ic = (1/N_ic) sum |u_theta(0, x_i) - g(x_i)|^2 (Eq. 2.6); L_bc = (1/N_bc) sum |B[u_theta]|^2 (Eq. 2.7); L_r = (1/M) sum_{i=1}^M w_i L_r^i(theta), L_r^i = mean square residual of the i-th temporal segment (Eq. 2.10), w_i = exp(-eps sum_{k=1}^{i-1} L_r^k) (Eq. 2.11); multi-term splits for Stokes/NS (u/v components, inflow, outflow, no-slip, momentum, continuity residuals per Figs. 21, 24, 25)
loss_weighting: self-adaptive, two schemes: (a) gradient-norm based (default first choice): lambda_ic = sum of all gradient L2 norms / ||Grad L_ic||, similarly lambda_bc, lambda_r (Eq. 2.12-2.14), updated every f=1000 steps with moving average alpha=0.9; (b) NTK-based using only diagonal NTK entries (Eq. 5.7-5.9), more stable but costlier; plus causal temporal weights with tolerance eps=1.0 (default f=1000, alpha=0.9, gamma=1.0, eps=1.0; weights frozen w.r.t. theta); defaults: all weights initialized to 1
sampling_strategy: uniform random sampling of collocation points at every iteration; batch size 4096 for ablation studies, 8192 in best hyper-parameter configurations (40960 per GPU for multi-GPU weak scaling); authors strongly recommend random over full-batch sampling to avoid overfitting the PDE residuals and reduce memory; no adaptive RAD/RAR sampling used
optimizer_schedule: Adam only (no L-BFGS anywhere); initial learning rate 0.001 with exponential decay rate 0.9 every 2000 decay steps (5000 decay steps for Allen-Cahn); total iterations 1e5-3e5 for single-shot problems; time-marching windows: KS 10 windows x 2e5 steps/window, NS torus 5 windows x 1.5e5, NS cylinder 10 windows x 2e5; lid-driven cavity curriculum Re=[100,400,1000,3200] with [5e4, 5e4, 1e5, 5e5] iterations; Adam recommended over tuned optimizers; weight decay not recommended for forward problems; hyper-parameter sweeps over learning-rate schedules, network sizes, activations performed for best results
training_compute: GPU(s), JAX framework with automatic data-parallel multi-GPU training; demonstrated weak scaling up to 256 GPUs (NS torus benchmark, batch 40960 per GPU, 10000 iterations, ~87-100% parallel efficiency, Fig. 2); run times (min) reported per ablation: e.g. Allen-Cahn full pipeline 16.26 min vs plain 12.93 min; advection 9.18 min; Stokes 9.51 min; KS 13.33 min; cavity full 58.86 min; specific GPU model not stated
domain_decomposition: temporal decomposition only (no spatial subdomains): (a) M equal temporal segments for causal weighting (16 or 32 chunks in configs); (b) curriculum/time-marching: temporal domain split into 5 (torus) or 10 (KS, cylinder) windows, prediction from the last time step of the previous window used as initial condition for the next; noted as a temporal domain decomposition strategy that reduces optimization difficulty but increases computational cost
transfer_or_pretraining: curriculum training for singularly perturbed / high-Re problems: model trained at lower Reynolds number used as initialization for higher Re (lid-driven cavity Re sequence 100->400->1000->3200); for NS cylinder a zero solution from a coarse 4-second numerical simulation serves as the starting initial condition
data_regime: physics-only (no data) for training: PDE residual + IC + BC losses only; validation against reference solutions (numerical solvers / exact solutions; Ghia et al. 1982 centerline velocity profiles for cavity); one coarse numerical simulation used only to build the IC for the cylinder case
datasets_used: Allen-Cahn equation; advection equation (c=80); Stokes flow in pipe with circular cylinder (Re=20); Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation (alpha=100/16, beta=100/16^2, gamma=100/16^4); lid-driven cavity (Re=3200, Ghia et al. reference); Navier-Stokes flow in a torus (Re=100, T=10); Navier-Stokes flow around a cylinder (Re=100)
baselines_compared: conventional/plain PINN formulation (Raissi et al.) as the 'Plain' ablation baseline in every benchmark; internal ablations disabling one pipeline component at a time; Ghia et al. 1982 multigrid Navier-Stokes solution for the cavity; numerical reference solutions for the other cases; Chuang & Barba 2022 report (claiming PINNs act as steady-flow solvers and fail to capture vortex shedding) explicitly challenged
evaluation_metrics: relative L^2 error against reference solution; run time (min); gradient histograms of back-propagated losses, NTK eigenvalue spectra (K_ic, K_r), temporal residual loss L_r(t), and min_i w_i(t) convergence as training diagnostics; parallel efficiency (%) for weak scaling
key_quantitative_results: Table 1 state-of-the-art rel. L^2 errors of the proposed pipeline: Allen-Cahn 5.37e-5; advection (c=80) 6.88e-4; Stokes flow 8.04e-5; Kuramoto-Sivashinsky 1.61e-1 (error concentrated in last time steps); lid-driven cavity (Re=3200) 1.58e-1 vs Ghia et al.; NS flow in torus 2.45e-1 at T=10; NS cylinder: test error not reported. Ablations (full pipeline vs disabled component): Allen-Cahn full 5.84e-4 vs no-Fourier 4.35e-1 and plain 5.174e-1; advection full 1.02e-2 vs plain 9.51e-1; Stokes full (with non-dimensionalization) 5.41e-4 vs 9.74e-1 without it; KS full 1.42e-4 vs no-modified-MLP 2.98e-3 and plain 2.59e-1; cavity full 1.34e-1 vs plain 7.94e-1. Weak scaling to 256 GPUs demonstrated
errors_reported: Allen-Cahn: rel L2 = 5.37e-5 (best), 5.84e-4 (default Algorithm 1), 4.35e-1 (no Fourier features), 6.62e-3 (no RWF), 7.51e-3 (no grad norm), 1.59e-3 (no causal), 5.174e-1 (plain). Advection (c=80): 6.88e-4 (best), 1.02e-2 (default), 4.29e-1 (no Fourier), 1.31e-2 (no grad norm), 1.13e-2 (no causal), 1.49e-2 (no time period), 9.51e-1 (plain). Stokes: 8.04e-5 (best), 5.41e-4 (default), 9.56e-1 (no Fourier), 9.86e-1 (no RWF), 1.01e-2 (no grad norm), 9.74e-1 (no non-dimensionalization), error vs ||u||_2 = sqrt(u^2+v^2). KS: 1.61e-1 (best/default 1.42e-4), 2.98e-3 (no modified MLP), 1.86e-2 (no Fourier, no RWF rows), 2.19e-1 (no grad norm), 2.58e-4 (no causal), 2.59e-1 (plain). Lid-driven cavity: 1.58e-1 (best, Re=3200), 1.34e-1 (default full), 7.32e-1 (no Fourier), 1.59e-1 (no RWF), 3.38e-1 (no grad norm), 5.48e-1 (no modified MLP), 7.94e-1 (plain); error grows with Re (~0.5 at Re=1000, ~0.5 at Re=3200 direct). NS torus: 2.45e-1 at T=10
speedup_claims: no direct speedup vs numerical solvers claimed; RWF (from prior work [61]) said to 'consistently accelerate training convergence and enable more accurate results'; jaxpi claimed highly optimized with weak scaling up to 256 GPUs enabling large-scale simulation; time-marching/curriculum explicitly acknowledged to increase computational cost (sequential training of multiple PINN models); plain PINN has shorter run time than full pipeline (e.g. 12.93 vs 16.26 min Allen-Cahn) but far worse accuracy
ablations: systematic one-component-at-a-time ablations on every benchmark (Tables 2-5, 11): components tested = Fourier features, RWF, gradient-norm weighting, causal weighting, non-dimensionalization (Stokes, cavity), time-periodicity (advection), modified MLP (KS, cavity). Findings: every component contributes positively; removing Fourier features is the most damaging for Allen-Cahn (4.35e-1) and advection (4.29e-1); removing non-dimensionalization devastates Stokes (9.74e-1 vs 5.41e-4); removing modified MLP hurts KS most (2.98e-3 vs 1.42e-4); removing causal weighting degrades Allen-Cahn (1.59e-3) and KS (2.58e-4 -> 2.59e-1 for plain); ablation settings differ from the tuned settings used for best results
stated_limitations: non-dimensionalization is 'not a silver bullet' since PDE residual scales can still differ (Sec. 3); the spectral information needed to choose Fourier sigma is not accessible when solving forward PDEs, so sigma in [1,10] recommended empirically (Sec. 4.2); causal residual loss is sensitive to eps: too small eps forces conventional-PINN behavior, too large eps makes optimization harder and may be infeasible with limited network capacity; min_i w_i(t) should converge to 1 else reduce eps (Sec. 5.1); gradient-based weights less stable than NTK-based due to noisy mini-batch gradients, but NTK is costlier (Sec. 5.2); time-marching increases computational cost as multiple PINN models are trained sequentially (Sec. 5.3, 7.4); one-shot KS training error grows drastically with final time T (Fig. 12) and discrepancies near t=1 attributed to error accumulation and chaos (Sec. 7.4); PINNs trained directly at high Re are unstable and converge to erroneous solutions, motivating curriculum (Sec. 7.5); for NS cylinder test error is not reported because 'numerical solvers fluctuate based on the underlying discretizations', and >10 loss terms make manual weight tuning practically infeasible (Sec. 7.7)
failure_modes: spectral bias toward low frequencies (diagnosed via NTK eigenvalue decay); unbalanced back-propagated gradients across loss terms (PDE-residual gradients dominate); violation of temporal causality (network minimizes residuals at later times first); overfitting of PDE residuals with full-batch training; training instability / convergence to erroneous solutions at high Reynolds numbers (Re > ~1000 direct training); failure to capture vortex shedding reported by prior work (Chuang & Barba) and here attributed to improper PINN usage; sharp transitions between trained and untrained temporal windows visible in multi-window training (Figs. 22, 24, 25)
reproducibility: code publicly available at https://github.com/PredictiveIntelligenceLab/jaxpi (JAX-based 'highly optimized' library); full hyper-parameter configurations published for all benchmarks (Tables 6-13: architecture, training, weighting parameters); training animations on the GitHub page; ablation settings documented; random seeds and hardware model not stated; diagnostics (gradient norms, NTK eigenvalues) built into the library
quotable_finding: We show that the methods and guiding principles put forth in this study lead to state-of-the-art results, and provide strong baselines that future studies should use for comparison purposes. (p.1, abstract)
relevance_rqs: RQ2: core evidence on PINN components (Fourier features, RWF, modified MLP, grad-norm/NTK weighting, causal weights, non-dimensionalization, curriculum) with ablation-quantified contributions; RQ3: physics+mechanism evidence (autodiff residual soft-penalty vs hard periodic-BC Fourier construction, and when each matters); RQ4: reliability evidence (systematic diagnosis of spectral bias, unbalanced gradients, causality violation; reproducible baselines and failure diagnostics); RQ1 partially (forward PDE problem classes, mostly fluids)
manuscript_section: S4 (methods: training pipeline, loss weighting, architectures, enforcement); T2/T3 (component/technique tables and benchmark error table); failure-modes and reliability discussion in the reliability section
cross_paper_links: builds-on: PINN-A01 (Raissi et al. 2019, original PINN formulation followed in Sec. 2); PINN-A06 (Wang, Yu & Perdikaris 2021 'When PINNs fail to train' NTK view - NTK weighting Eq. 5.4-5.9 and eigenvalue diagnostics); PINN-A07 (McClenny & Bruga-Netta self-adaptive weights - cited [28] in the loss-reweighting line). builds-on named: Wang, Sankaran & Perdikaris 2022 causality paper arXiv:2307.04664 (causal weighting, ref [53]); Wang et al. 2022 random weight factorization (ref [61]); Wang, Teng & Perdikaris 2021 gradient-flow pathologies / modified MLP (ref [26]); Krishnapriyan et al. 2021 curriculum training (ref [48]); Dong & Ni 2021 exact periodic BCs (ref [64]); Tancik et al. 2020 Fourier features (ref [60]); Sukumar & Srivastava 2021 and Lu et al. 2021 hard BC imposition (refs [65,66]). contradicts: Chuang & Barba 2022 (ref [69]) - shows PINNs can capture vortex shedding. compares-to: Ghia et al. 1982 reference cavity solution (ref [68])
notes_caveats: Preprint (later widely cited as the reference PINN-training guide accompanying jaxpi). Best-case numbers come from extensive hyper-parameter sweeps while ablations use a fixed default configuration, so ablation rows and Table 1 numbers are not directly comparable (authors note this). All seven benchmarks are forward, physics-only math benchmarks - no experimental data, no FEM/FVM runtime or accuracy comparison, no inverse problems, no UQ. KS (1.61e-1), cavity (1.58e-1) and torus (2.45e-1) relative errors are large despite 'state-of-the-art' framing. Cylinder case reports no quantitative error (discretization-dependent vortex shedding); the 'first empirical evidence of PINN vortex shedding' claim is qualitative. Strong candidate for the survey's methods/training-strategy backbone given exhaustive ablations and released code
